factsAccepted: Comparable-store sales declined 7% YoY in FY2025, the third consecutive year of negative comps. The decline decomposes cleanly: store traffic fell 9% YoY while conversion held roughly flat (stable low-to-mid-teens %) and average ticket rose ~1%. Because conversion and ticket are stable, the comp decline is almost entirely a traffic problem — fewer customers choosing to visit — rather than a failure to convert or an in-store execution issue. This is the signature of declining demand for / relevance of the format, not an operational breakdown at the point of sale.

Inventory write-downs and markdown reserves rose from $9M (1.4% of revenue) in FY2024 to $24M (4.0% of revenue) in FY2025 — a 260 bps increase in the write-down rate and a 167% increase in absolute dollars. The escalation indicates the company is repeatedly buying merchandise that customers do not purchase at full price and is forced to mark it down. The write-down rate is the clearest financial signal that the assortment is misaligned with what the customer base wants, and it is the primary driver of the gross-margin compression.

E-commerce grew to 18% of sales ($108M) in FY2025, up from 12% ($77M) the prior year, yet total revenue still fell 6.5% (from $642M to $600M). Store sales declined faster than e-commerce grew, so the online channel is not offsetting store losses. Combined with flat conversion in stores, this pattern indicates net share loss and channel cannibalization — existing customers shifting some spend online while the company loses total wallet — rather than additive digital growth that expands the customer base.

Gross margin compressed from 38% to 34% (400 bps) in FY2025, with the majority of the decline attributable to the increase in markdowns/write-downs (write-down rate up ~260 bps, from 1.4% to 4.0% of revenue), and the remainder to occupancy de-leverage and channel/mix effects. EBITDA fell from $45M (7.0% margin) to $24M (4.0% margin), a ~300 bps decline. With high leverage and a refinancing due within 90-120 days, the EBITDA erosion is narrowing covenant headroom; another heavy markdown season threatens a covenant breach.

Roughly 6 of 30 stores are EBITDA-negative on a four-wall basis, and occupancy cost is rising as a percentage of declining store sales (operating de-leverage). Long lease terms (5-12 years remaining, with early-termination penalties) make rapid fleet exit costly. While the four-wall losses and occupancy de-leverage are real and worsen the financials, they are a consequence of falling store sales rather than an independent cost shock — fixed occupancy is being spread over a shrinking sales base driven by the traffic decline.
factsNeedingClarification: Lapsed-customer and competitive-defection research: where former customers now shop (off-price, specialty, pure-play online) and why they stopped — not currently collected.
Brand-perception / relevance study: how target and lapsed customers rate the banner on differentiation, value, assortment, and reasons-to-visit versus competitors.

Category-level and SKU-level markdown root-cause data: which categories/buys drove the write-down increase, and whether it was over-buying, assortment misfit, or pricing — public/aggregate data masks this.
Customer overlap between store and e-commerce: degree to which online sales are existing store customers shifting channel (cannibalization) versus genuinely incremental customers.
Competitor pricing, traffic, and assortment benchmarks at the local-market level for each of the 30 stores.
